problem_text:
A logistics company is selecting cargo containers to load onto a transport vehicle. Available containers are:
* Container 1: size 34 cubic meters, revenue $153
* Container 2: size 27 cubic meters, revenue $120
* Container 3: size 33 cubic meters, revenue $62
* Container 4: size 49 cubic meters, revenue $195
* Container 5: size 41 cubic meters, revenue $180
* Container 6: size 17 cubic meters, revenue $270
* Container 7: size 15 cubic meters, revenue $265
* Container 8: size 38 cubic meters, revenue $118
* Container 9: size 37 cubic meters, revenue $36
* Container 10: size 37 cubic meters, revenue $65
* Container 11: size 17 cubic meters, revenue $231
* Container 12: size 42 cubic meters, revenue $61
* Container 13: size 3 cubic meters, revenue $61
* Container 14: size 21 cubic meters, revenue $179
* Container 15: size 8 cubic meters, revenue $154
* Container 16: size 7 cubic meters, revenue $133
* Container 17: size 20 cubic meters, revenue $43
* Container 18: size 7 cubic meters, revenue $210
* Container 19: size 31 cubic meters, revenue $86
* Container 20: size 21 cubic meters, revenue $125
* Container 21: size 9 cubic meters, revenue $131
* Container 22: size 9 cubic meters, revenue $30
* Container 23: size 46 cubic meters, revenue $37
* Container 24: size 30 cubic meters, revenue $254

The vehicle has a maximum capacity of 419 cubic meters. Choose the container combination that maximizes total revenue without exceeding this capacity limit. Each container must be either fully accepted or rejected.
